03 / FROM CURIOUS TO CONTRIBUTINGTHREE SMALL STEPS

You bring the curiosity.
We’ll bring the context.

01

Open a repository.

CONTRI recognizes the GitHub project you’re viewing. No copy-paste routine, no full-width dashboard.

02

Read the evidence.

See the overview first. Open Team for response patterns or Issues to inspect contribution opportunities.

03

Start a conversation.

Read the project’s guide and issue discussion. Check existing work. Then bring your idea to the community.

YOUR NEXT STEP, PREPARED

Bring your curiosity.
And your favorite AI.

01

Keep a shortlist.

Save promising issues and projects with private local notes. Compare recent activity across up to three saved projects.

02

Prepare a contribution brief.

Gather source links, reference-check results, and a before-you-start checklist. Review what you want help with.

03

Copy. Open. Explore.

Paste the brief into ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or your preferred chat. Nothing is sent automatically. Your provider’s limits apply; an API subscription is not required for copying.

A FEW FIELD NOTES

Good questions.
Clear answers.

Is CONTRI free?+

Yes. The source is available under the MIT license. You can inspect it, improve it, and build on it.

Do I need a GitHub token?+

Anonymous mode works within GitHub’s public API limits. An optional public-read token increases capacity. The extension includes a walkthrough and defaults to session-only token storage. GitHub’s limits still apply.

Can it tell me every maintainer?+

No. It shows observed team responders using public owner, member, and collaborator labels. The roster and activity samples may be incomplete; each result explains its coverage.

Does “no linked open PR” mean an issue is free?+

No. It means no open PR was found in the completed public-reference check. Someone may have unlinked work. Always read the discussion and coordinate with the project.

What stays on my device?+

Public report caches, your explicitly saved shortlist and notes, widget position, and optionally your token. There is no analytics or application backend. Tokens go only to GitHub. The full privacy policy is in the repository.

Is it on the Chrome Web Store?+

Not yet. CONTRI is in development. You can build and load the source locally. A packaged release will follow installed-extension verification.

YOUR NEXT CONTRIBUTION STARTS SOMEWHERE

Make it a
meaningful one.

CONTRI is taking shape in the open.
Try the development build, share feedback, or help build what comes next.

Get the development build ↗
  1. Clone the repository and run npm ci, then npm run build.
  2. Open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, and choose Load unpacked.
  3. Select the generated dist folder. Open a public GitHub repository.
  4. Use Settings inside CONTRI for optional token setup. Never share your token.

Requires Chrome 124 or newer. Development build; not a Chrome Web Store release.
